theater: 宋州睢陽城與汴河漕道

battle.name: 睢陽之戰
battle.theater: 宋州睢陽城與汴河漕道
battle.brief: 至德二載（757）十月至十二月，安史叛軍大將尹子奇率一萬三千眾圍攻河南道宋州睢陽，守將張巡與太守許遠合六千八百人當之，憑城堞與汴河之險力守逾百日。城中以枯木架木砲，拋礫石擊敵陣，焚撞車、拒雲梯；援兵不至而糧盡，城破之日張巡等三十六名將士不屈而死，睢陽旋為官軍收復。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 交戰一方是唐王朝河南道宋州的守軍。安史之亂起，張巡起兵於雍丘，屢挫叛軍，隨後奉詔與宋州太守許遠合守睢陽，兩人共節制城內兵六千八百人，兵源兼有郡兵、團練與臨時募來的散卒，分由四面城樓分守。糧秣原本靠江淮租稅沿汴河北運至宋州，再由睢陽轉輸洛陽，城外的糧倉、橋樑與渡口都派兵看守；上游斷絕之後，朝廷仍設法以小船運糧入城，但只有少量趁隙送到。另一方是安慶緒建立的偽齊（燕）政權之下大將尹子奇所部，起初領一萬三千眾西來，圍城之後屢得安慶緒從陳留方向增兵，總數增至數萬，並把洛陽、陳留、汴州一段的漕運線握在手中。叛軍的算盤很清楚：睢陽是汴河上的樞紐，此城一下，江淮的鹽、粟、衣料便可直抵洛陽，叛軍還可以東接河北的史思明。守軍方面的援助者則各自割據：河南節度使賀蘭泫等奉詔救援，卻各有私兵而不肯出師；河北道顏真卿義軍與朔方軍在北方拉住叛軍主力，也無法打通南下之路。睢陽一城因此不是兩軍對峙，而是被分割在唐廷、偽齊與各節度使三方之間的孤立支點。
countriesEn: One side was the Tang garrison of Songzhou in Henan Circuit. After the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Zhang Xun raised troops at Yongqiu, beat back the rebels several times, and was then appointed to hold Suiyang together with the governor of Songzhou, Xu Yuan. The two of them between them commanded 6,800 men inside the city, drawn from the local militia, the tuanlian levies and scattered men hastily recruited, and they were distributed to the four sides of the wall. The grain and clothing had originally come up from Jianghuai by the Bian canal to Songzhou and were then shifted north from Suiyang toward Luoyang; the depots, bridges and fords outside the city were all guarded. Once the upper reaches were cut off, the court still tried to bring grain in by small boats, but only a little slipped through at the gaps. The other side was the army of Yin Ziqi, a general of the false Qi (Yan) state established by An Qingxu. He led thirteen thousand men west at first and, after the city was invested, repeatedly received reinforcements from Anqingxu in the direction of Chenliu, raising the total to several tens of thousands, while holding the line of the canal from Luoyang through Chenliu to Binzhou. The rebel arithmetic was plain: Suiyang was the pivot of the Bian canal, and once it fell the salt, grain and cloth of Jianghuai could flow straight to Luoyang, while the rebels could also join hands with Shi Siming in Hebei to the east. Those who should have aided the garrison were themselves partitioned: the Henan jiedushi He Lanxian and others were ordered to send relief but each kept his own troops and would not march; the Hebei volunteers of Yan Zhenqing and the Shuofang army held the main rebel force in the north but could not open a road south. Suiyang was therefore not a two-sided confrontation but an isolated pivot cut off between three parties: the Tang court, the false Qi and the separate jiedushi.
people: 睢陽的守方以張巡為核心。他是蒲州人，先後任清河令、真源令，治政嚴整；安史亂後他起兵守雍丘，擊退令狐潮部，聲名漸起，被授為睢陽城守。他到睢陽後迅速查清城防、軍械、糧秣的實際數目，把六千八百人分派到四面城頭，規定分段輪值，並明令不許出城作無把握之戰；這在當時是很特別的做法，因為多數郡兵已乘夜逃散，張巡卻靠嚴明軍紀把殘兵練成能打的守軍。與他合守的是宋州太守許遠，許遠入城時留下自己的一部分兵給張巡，兩人自此共用一城。部將之中，南霽雲以射藝聞名，多次射傷敵將，曾突圍向河南節度使賀蘭泫求援，肯以斷指明志，終於換來援軍；雷萬春守城東面，身中數矢而屹立不動，穩住了最易被突破的一面。敵方主帥尹子奇是偽齊宿將，攻城不下，屢次遣人勸降，又調集雲梯、撞車強攻。更高的層面上，朔方軍主將郭子儀、李光弼收復兩京是全局的關鍵；宰相房琯與張巡早年同在陳州任上便結怨，此後朝議與援兵調度仍受其影響。
peopleEn: The heart of the Suiyang defense was Zhang Xun. A native of Puzhou, he had served as magistrate of Qinghe and later of Zhenyuan and governed with strict discipline; after the rebellion broke out he raised troops at Yongqiu and beat back the force of Linghu Chao, and his reputation grew until he was appointed to the defense of Suiyang. On arriving he quickly established the real state of the walls, the arms and the stores, distributed the 6,800 men among the four sides of the city, laid down a system of rotating watches, and forbade any sally he could not guarantee; this was an unusual way to fight at the time, because most of the local militia had already slipped away in the night, and it was Zhang Xun's strict military discipline that turned the survivors into a garrison that could actually fight. He shared the city with Xu Yuan, the governor of Songzhou, who brought part of his own troops into the town when he took it over, and from then on the two men held the city in common. Among the commanders, Nan Jieyun was famous for his archery and wounded enemy officers more than once; he broke out of the siege to ask the Henan jiedushi He Lanxian for troops, was willing to cut off his own finger to show his resolve, and in the end did bring aid; Lei Wanchun held the east face, took several arrows and did not move, and steadied the side most likely to be broken. The rebel commander in chief was Yin Ziqi, a veteran of the false Qi. Unable to take the city, he sent envoys to call for surrender again and again and massed scaling ladders and battering rams for a forced assault. At the higher level, the recovery of the two capitals by Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi of the Shuofang army was the key to the war as a whole; and the chancellor Fang Guan, who had already fallen out with Zhang Xun when they both held office in Chenzhou, continued to shape the court's deliberations and the dispatch of relief.
kits: 這件兵器是投石機，即西方所稱的 onager，羅馬式的扭索發射機：靠絞索與槓桿的扭力把石彈拋出，最早見於公元前二世紀末的羅馬軍，後來成為希臘羅馬軍攻城與野戰的標準火力。它的價值在於把人工的勢能換成一次爆發的破壞力，不必依靠弓臂的持久拉力，一發可以打穿屋頂、砸塌城堞，或在密集隊形上砸出一個缺口。中國自東漢末、三國以來已有類似的發石車，曹操、袁紹都曾使用，隋唐之際投石機在軍中已與雲梯、撞車、飛樓、巢車並列，《唐六典》與《太白陰經》都收錄了砲的形制與用法。睢陽城頭那一批卻是應急改裝：張巡缺器械，便以城內枯木架成木砲，取汴河河灘的礫石作彈丸，《新唐書·張巡傳》記木砲「中其人常兩人洞穿」。這種臨時器械優點是就地取材、補充迅速，缺點是壽命短、射程近，難以壓制遠處密集的雲梯，因此只能配合弓弩與火攻使用，不能單獨決定戰局。叛軍同樣用投石機與撞車壓迫城牆，並以寬數丈、可載數百壯士的雲梯貼壁。守軍對付雲梯的辦法是弓弩俯射、以火箭與燃燒物焚燒梯體和撞車，並在城頭以拒馬與礫石堵住攀城之路。當時火藥在唐已為人所知，但仍以點火、煙霧與燃燒用途為主，把火藥裝進炮膛作爆炸彈丸是宋代以後的事，故睢陽之戰仍屬純機械破壞力的年代。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the stone-throwing engine known in the West as the onager, the Roman torsion machine that hurls a stone shot by the twist of sinews and levers. It first appears in the Roman army of the late third century BC and later became standard firepower for Greek and Roman armies in siege and in the field. Its value is that it converts human effort into a single burst of destructive force; it does not depend on the sustained pull of a bow limb, and one shot can punch through a roof, break down a parapet or tear a hole in a crowded formation. China had comparable stone-throwing carts from the late Han and the Three Kingdoms onward, used by Cao Cao and by Yuan Shao, and by the Sui and Tang the engine stood in the army alongside scaling ladders, battering rams, flying towers and siege towers, with the Tangliudian and the Taibai Yinjing both recording the form and the use of the pao. The machines on the walls of Suiyang, however, were emergency improvisations: lacking proper equipment, Zhang Xun built wooden throwers out of dead timber from inside the city and used the cobbles of the Bian riverbank as shot, and the Xinshu biography of Zhang Xun records that a wooden pao 'passed through two men at a time where it struck.' Such makeshift engines had the advantage of being built from what was to hand and easily replaced, and the disadvantage of short life and short range, so that they could not break up distant masses of scaling ladders; they had to be used together with bows and crossbows and with fire, and could not decide the battle alone. The rebels used stone-throwers and battering rams in their turn to press on the walls, and brought scaling ladders several zhang wide, wide enough to carry several hundred brave men, up against the masonry. The garrison met them with crossbow and arrow fire from above, with fire arrows and incendiaries against the ladders and the rams, and with cheval-de-frise and rubble blocking the ways up the wall. Gunpowder was known in the Tang, but was still used for ignition, smoke and burning; loading it into a gun barrel as an explosive shot only came later, in the Song, so the Battle of Suiyang belongs to an age of purely mechanical destructive power.
tactics: 守方的打法全部圍繞城牆與糧道。張巡進城先做三件事：清點兵械，把可用之數報給朝廷；把守軍分四面專責，各將守一段；把糧食登記，禁將士隨意取用。對外他不主動出城，只在夜裡選叛軍新到、營壘未固或器械密集的時機出擊，曾夜襲敵營破其一軍、掠回攻城器械，使叛軍攻勢屢屢重整。敵人密集在牆下時，就以木砲拋礫石，射擊擁擠的攻梯隊列；雲梯逼近牆頭，就用弓弩集中封住攀城者，點燃梯上的柴草，把火勢引回敵陣。叛軍在箭雨與火攻下屢攻不克，改為長期圍困，試圖斷城內糧水，逼守軍自潰。城內糧食耗盡後，守軍把射出的箭桿、鎧甲部件煮食充飢，仍未潰散。攻方則分兵遮斷自北面與東面來的援軍，只留一部主攻城寨，同時保住通往洛陽的糧道，使唐廷的援兵無法接近；每攻不下一次便增兵一次，直至援軍抵達。城區在大雨中井泉皆溢，守軍需以木為筏通行與調動，守軍在城頭與城下的空間被水與圍困同時壓縮，這是雙方都受限的環境。
tacticsEn: Everything the defenders did turned on the wall and on the grain road. On entering the city Zhang Xun first did three things: he took stock of the arms and reported the usable numbers to the court; he assigned the garrison to the four sides, each officer responsible for one stretch; and he had the stores registered and forbade the troops to take from them at will. Outwardly he did not sortie, but chose his night attacks by careful timing: when the rebels had just arrived, when their camp was not yet consolidated, or when their siege equipment was crowded together. He once fell on the enemy camp by night, broke one of their units and carried off their siege engines, so that the rebel assault had to be assembled again and again. When the enemy massed under the wall he threw cobbles with the wooden pao into the crowded columns around the ladders; when the ladders came within reach of the parapet he concentrated bow and crossbow fire on the men climbing and set fire to the brushwood lashed to them, throwing the flames back into the enemy formation. After repeated failures under arrow and fire the rebels changed to a long blockade, trying to cut off grain and water inside the wall and force the garrison to break. When the food in the city ran out the soldiers boiled the shafts of spent arrows and pieces of their own armor to eat, and still did not dissolve. On the attacking side, troops were posted to interdict relief coming from the north and the east, with only a detachment left to press the siege, while the road to Luoyang was kept open so that the Tang supplies could reach them; every failed assault was followed by an increase in the besieging force, right up to the arrival of the relief army. During heavy rain the wells and springs inside the city overflowed and the defenders had to move on rafts of timber; the usable space on and below the walls was compressed at once by water and by siege, and the environment limited both sides alike.
data: 數字方面最常被引用的有兩組：守軍六千八百人，叛軍主攻兵力一萬三千。兩組數字都出自《資治通鑑》記睢陽圍城：張巡與許遠合守睢陽，「兵共六千八百人」，而尹子奇「將兵萬三千」。此後叛軍續有增兵，實際交戰兵力當然高於此數，但史書未留下確切總數，不宜再加推算。守城時間通常記為逾百日：自至德二載（757）十月合圍到十二月城破，約三個月。城為夯土所築，周圍數里，牆高數丈，開四門並有通往城內的門道。器械方面，叛軍所造雲梯寬數丈、可載數百壯士，一次備齊即逼近牆下；守軍的木砲以數十斤重的礫石為彈，中人則兩人洞穿。守軍最終減員到數百之數，具體人數不詳；城破之日，張巡、許遠等三十六名將士同死而不降，這個數目見於《新唐書·張巡傳》，是本戰最常被引用的損失數字。尹子奇一度久攻不下而思退，張巡夜襲破敵一軍、奪回攻城器械，才迫其再攻。城破之後，叛軍搜捕殘部，張巡、許遠等人被殺於城中，其後屍身受辱的說法見於後世筆記，諸說並存，未可盡信。
dataEn: As for numbers, the two most often cited are the 6,800 defenders and the 13,000 principal rebel troops; both come from the Zizhi Tongjian's account of the siege of Suiyang, which says that Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan together held the city with '6,800 men in all' and that Yin Ziqi 'led thirteen thousand men.' Reinforcements continued to arrive afterwards, so the actual force engaged was certainly larger, but the histories give no exact total and it would be unsafe to add any estimate of our own. The length of the defense is usually given as somewhat more than a hundred days: from the complete investment in the tenth month of the second year of Zhide (757) to the fall of the city in the twelfth month, about three months. The wall was rammed earth, several li in circuit, several zhang high, with four gates and passages leading into the town. On the materiel side, the rebels' scaling ladders were several zhang wide and could carry several hundred armed men, and a single set brought up would reach the wall; the defenders' wooden pao threw cobbles of several tens of jin, passing through two men where they struck. The garrison was finally reduced to some several hundred, the exact figure being unknown; on the day the city fell Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan and thirty-five other officers died rather than surrender, and that number is recorded in the Xinshu biography of Zhang Xun and is the loss figure most often quoted for this battle. Yin Ziqi at one point thought of withdrawing because the siege went badly, and it was only a night attack that broke one of his units and took back the siege engines which forced him to press on. After the city was carried, the rebels hunted down the remnants, and Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan and the others were killed inside the walls; the stories of what was done to their bodies afterwards come from later notes and vary, and cannot be taken as certain.
cause: 睢陽之戰是安史之亂由河北打到江淮的產物，也是唐廷在兩京失守之後的第一次戰略反撲。亂軍首領安祿山於天寶十四載（755）起兵，次年攻陷洛陽與長安，玄宗西入蜀地，肅宗在靈武即位；河南道作為江淮糧道與洛陽之間的通道，立刻成為叛軍必爭之地。尹子奇西進的算盤很清楚：睢陽是汴河上的樞紐，此城一下，江淮的粟、鹽、衣料便可直抵洛陽，佔了睢陽，叛軍還可以東接河北的史思明，西壓唐廷的江淮。守方則是被推上來的。起義之前，張巡在雍丘以寡兵破令狐潮部，聲名漸起；朝廷在睢陽的郡兵與團練早已潰散，許遠到任時只剩老弱，張巡到後收攏散卒、重整城防，把一所空城變成可以死守的堡壘。真正把守軍推向絕境的是兩件外部的事：一是叛軍控制了汴河以北的上游，睢陽的南面是江淮、北面是洛陽與陳留，城池正卡在這條南北漕運的咽喉上，一旦失守，江淮的物資就要改道，朝廷在河南的軍隊也失去糧源；二是朝廷自身的失序，節度使擁兵自重、彼此不相統屬，宰相房琯雖奉詔出兵而無力駕馭諸軍，睢陽遂成孤城。
causeEn: The Battle of Suiyang was a product of the An Lushan rebellion spreading from Hebei into Jianghuai, and was the Tang court's first strategic counterstroke after the loss of the two capitals. The leader of the revolt, An Lushan, rose in the fourteenth year of Tianbao (755); the next year Luoyang and Chang'an fell, the Xuanzong emperor fled west into Shu, and the Suzong emperor was enthroned at Lingwu. Henan Circuit, the corridor between the Jianghuai grain road and Luoyang, at once became a point that the rebels had to hold. Yin Ziqi's arithmetic going west was plain: Suiyang was the pivot of the Bian canal, and once the city fell the grain, salt and cloth of Jianghuai could run straight to Luoyang; holding Suiyang the rebels could also join hands with Shi Siming in Hebei to the east and press down on the Tang's Jianghuai from the west. The defenders were pushed into the position rather than seeking it. Before the rising, Zhang Xun had broken Linghu Chao's force at Yongqiu with a handful of men and his name had grown; the militia and tuanlian of Suiyang had already disintegrated, and when Xu Yuan took up his post only the old and the weak remained, so that when Zhang Xun arrived, gathering stragglers and restoring the defenses turned an empty town into a place that could be held to the death. Two things outside the city pushed the garrison toward ruin. First, the rebels held the upper reaches of the Bian north of Suiyang: to the south of the city lay Jianghuai, to the north Luoyang and Chenliu, and the city sat exactly on the throat of that north-south grain route, so that if it fell the goods of Jianghuai had to go elsewhere and the Tang armies in Henan lost their food. Second, the court's own disorder: the jiedushi held their troops for themselves and were not subordinate to one another, and the chancellor Fang Guan, though he did dispatch troops on imperial orders, could not bring the various contingents under control, and Suiyang was left a lonely city.
impact: 睢陽的得失，牽動的是安史之亂整條南北運輸線。睢陽陷落之後，江淮的漕運斷了數月，泗州、宿州一線相繼淪陷，江南的租賦與鹽利無從北運，唐廷在華北的戰事失去補給，叛軍卻因佔了運道而取得江南的物資，這是叛軍在形勢上最順的一段。睢陽之守同時為官軍爭取了時間：郭子儀、李光弼率朔方軍在北方收復兩京，叛軍主力被史思明、尹子奇等部牽制在河南、山東一線，若沒有睢陽的九十餘日，等到兩京光復，叛軍主力或已盡數東調。另一層影響在人心與制度上：張巡、許遠、南霽雲與同城三十六名將士的死，讓「以孤城當強虜」成為唐人記憶中的忠義範本，唐廷其後追贈官爵並立祠祭祀，韓愈專為張巡作《張中丞傳後敘》，歷代文人屢以睢陽入詩。此後唐廷在江南加強漕運與江防，在河南則以重兵奪回睢陽，把這座城當作南北交通的關鍵節點經營，而不再只當作一個州城。睢陽失守與收復的這段經歷，成為安史之亂中少數以具體城池貫穿的完整戰例。
impactEn: What Suiyang decided was the whole north-south transport line of the rebellion. After the city fell the Jianghuai grain road was broken for months, Sizhou and Suzhou fell in turn, the rents and salt revenues of Jiangnan could no longer be carried north, the Tang lost the supply of their armies in northern China, while the rebels, holding the road, drew the products of Jiangnan to themselves; this was the one stretch in which the rebel offensive ran most smoothly. At the same time the defense of Suiyang bought the Tang time: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi with the Shuofang army recovered the two capitals in the north, and the main rebel force was pinned in Henan and Shandong by the armies of Shi Siming and Yin Ziqi; without the ninety-odd days of Suiyang, the rebel main body might have been shifted east in its entirety before the two capitals were retaken. A second effect lay in morale and in institutions: the deaths of Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Nan Jieyun and the thirty-six officers who died with them turned 'a lone city holding against a mighty host' into a model of loyalty in Tang memory; the court afterwards conferred titles and honours and raised shrines for them, Han Yu wrote the Account of the Sequel to the Biography of Constable Zhang for Zhang Xun, and men of letters in later ages again and again put Suiyang into verse. Thereafter the Tang strengthened the canal and the river defenses in Jiangnan, and in Henan they took Suiyang back with weighty forces and treated the city as a key node on the north-south traffic rather than as one more prefectural seat. The cycle of the fall and the recapture of Suiyang remains one of the few complete campaigns of the An Lushan rebellion told through a single walled city.
result: 直接結果是一城陷落、守將盡死。城破之日，張巡、許遠及同城三十六名將士被殺而不降；南霽雲被俘，押送洛陽，屢勸不聽，後得脫歸唐，朝廷亦為其立名追贈。援軍在城破後不久抵達睢陽城下，擊敗尹子奇大軍，尹子奇解圍夜遁，睢陽重歸朝廷，但此時城中已空，糧盡兵死，汴河漕道要重新打通才行。睢陽陷落之後數月，泗州、宿州相繼失守，江淮震動，叛軍攻勢看似達到頂點；但從全局看，兩京在至德二載（757）九、十月相繼被官軍收復，叛軍主力被史思明部的河北戰事與朔方軍釘在北方，攻勢此後轉入相持。睢陽的得失因此沒有改變安史之亂的總走向，卻明確標示出攻防兩條線的交叉點：它既暴露了唐廷在河南調度失靈、各節度使擁兵不法的痼疾，也以最慘烈的方式展示了當時唐軍在裝備、後勤與指揮上能達到的極限。張巡身後，睢陽的城與其廟祀成為唐代忠義的固定意象，歷代史書與文學反覆引用這一戰，作為衡量後來將領的尺子。
resultEn: The immediate result was the fall of the city and the death of its commanders. On the day the city was taken, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan and the thirty-six officers of the town were killed rather than surrender; Nan Jieyun was captured and carried off to Luoyang, refused every argument to surrender, and later escaped back to the Tang, and the court likewise gave him a name and posthumous honours. The relief army reached the foot of Suiyang shortly after the fall, broke Yin Ziqi's army, and Yin Ziqi lifted the siege and fled by night, so that Suiyang returned to the Tang; but the town was by then empty, its grain spent and its soldiers dead, and the canal road had to be reopened before anything could move again. In the months after Suiyang fell, Sizhou and Suzhou were lost in turn and Jianghuai was shaken, and the rebel offensive seemed to have reached its height; yet on the wider stage the two capitals were recovered by the Tang in the ninth and tenth months of the second year of Zhide (757), the rebel main body was pinned in the north by the Hebei war of Shi Siming's forces and by the Shuofang army, and the offensive settled into a stalemate. The outcome at Suiyang therefore did not change the general course of the rebellion, but it marked clearly the crossing point of the two lines of the war: it exposed the paralysis of the Tang's command in Henan and the endemic refusal of the jiedushi to put their troops under orders, and it showed in the most brutal way the limit of what a Tang army could achieve in equipment, supply and command. After Zhang Xun, the city of Suiyang and the shrines raised for him became a fixed image of loyalty in the Tang, and the historians and the writers of later ages cited this battle again and again as a yardstick with which to measure the generals who came after.
